iShares direct live validation on 2026-06-09 also confirmed the current IWM product-data JSON route returns 1913 holdings rows, so the remaining ETF-holdings breakage is persistence/page wiring rather than provider fetch reachability whenever IWM still looks empty in a local app state.

ETF constituent resolution now attempts identifier-driven provider enrichment by CUSIP/ISIN/SEDOL before placeholder fallback, and re-ingesting the same snapshot hash now reconciles already-stored placeholder constituent rows instead of leaving old HOLDING-* symbols frozen in place forever.
Baseline manual/admin legacy SEC N-Q/N-CSR-style XML/table and simple EDGAR HTML schedule-table reconstruction now exists as sec_legacy_reconstructed_holdings provenance.
Legacy SEC HTML parsing now supports split-row schedule tables where the security identity/CUSIP row is followed by a separate numeric shares/value/percent row.
Automated SEC legacy N-Q/N-CSR-style EDGAR discovery/download/backfill now exists with duplicate-safe accession state, single-ETF endpoint, bulk endpoint, and focused integration coverage.

SEC company_tickers_mf-style fund ticker discovery now exists through admin POST /api/v1/etf-holdings/discover-sec-funds; it materializes lightweight ETF instruments and upserts SEC CIK/series/class ids for EDGAR backfill routing, with optional source_url override and keyed-object/fields-data payload support.

Remaining ETF holdings work is still a major provider-native integration gap under the user's clarified standard: 231 of 345 registered providers do not yet have isolated native/live-backed issuer integrations. Separate downstream polish also remains for unusual issuer-specific schemas, non-tabular/PDF-like disclosures, automatic/broad issuer ETF discovery beyond explicit configured fund-list feeds, deeper dynamic point-in-time ETF attribution drilldowns, richer basket-history editing/import/rebalance policy UX, deeply nested/footnoted SEC HTML or PDF-like filings, saved ETF comparison sets/clustering UX on top of the overlap matrix API, and richer basket chart semantics.

Sprott now has a real provider-specific adapter backed by Sprott's public sitemap and product-page holdings discovery; live validation on 2026-06-10 confirmed NIKL returns parseable holdings rows through that route.

ETF constituent/provider enrichment now normalizes oversized exchange labels and long-form currency names before persisting lightweight/provider-enriched instruments, which fixes the EEM bootstrap `varchar(10)` / `varchar(3)` crashes seen in the backend traceback.

ETF bootstrap refresh now isolates issuer-route failures inside a nested transaction/savepoint so SEC fallback can continue cleanly instead of inheriting a poisoned SQLAlchemy session after a failed refresh attempt.

Expected yfinance quote misses encountered during best-effort ETF constituent enrichment are now logged at debug level rather than backend error level, reducing noisy false-alarm logs for fallback paths.

ETF bootstrap now reconciles the latest already-stored snapshot before returning it, so older QQQ-like holdings rows that were saved with identifiers but only placeholder symbols can now be promoted in place to real ticker-backed constituents without requiring a brand-new artifact ingestion.

ETF holdings ingestion now normalizes long-form holding-row currencies such as `Canada Dollar` to canonical codes like `CAD` before persisting snapshot rows, and SEC parsers normalize those values earlier too; this closes the `QQQJ` bootstrap crash class instead of leaving it as another symbol-specific failure.

The local EEM snapshots were repaired in no-network mode and post-repair verification showed bogus `SUGI` collisions dropped from 934 to 0.

The adapter fetches provider product pages such as JETS, parses the embedded public holdings table including mobile-label cell prefixes, extracts as-of dates, and is covered by static parser tests plus an opt-in live test.
